chunks: And it is narrated from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Rajab is a river in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever fasts one day from Rajab, Allah will give him to drink from that river."

key_terms.رَجَبٌ: Rajab, the seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting in the month of Rajab according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) characterizes Rajab as a celestial river in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, linking the spiritual purity of the month to its physical reward in the afterlife. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the high status of fasting even a single day in Rajab within Shia tradition, emphasizing divine generosity and the tangible rewards of devotion. The imagery of milk and honey serves as a metaphor for the sweetness of divine proximity and the purity of the soul achieved through worship.
